title: 17/23: Hand and finger injuries
description: Hand and finger injuries comprise almost a fifth of the incidents and events submitted by IMCA members just in the last year

title: 16/23: Crew member in small boat slipped and dislocated shoulder
description: A crew member kneeling down in a workboat was injured when the boat moved suddenly as a result of the sea state

title: 16/23: Small boat crew exposed to FPSO process water discharge (fumes and aerosol)
description: During diving operations on a live FPSO, the deck crew on the Light Dive Craft (LDC) and Fast Rescue Craft (FRC) were exposed to fumes and aerosols from the FPSO process water discharge

title: 16/23: LTI – Crew person cracked shin bone
description: An engineer suffered a broken shin when he slipped taking a shortcut into the engine room

title: 16/23: Person slipped on stairway while wearing shoe covers
description: While descending a vessel staircase in safety boots with company-approved shoe covers on, a person slipped down approximately four steps on the staircase. The person had a firm grip on the handrail at the time and thereby prevented further slippage. The strain of preventing a worse fall caused muscular pain on the left side of their torso and their left shoulder.

title: 16/23: BSEE: Lack of training with hydraulic torque wrench contributes to fatality
description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 459 relating to a fatality which occurred on a drillship in the Gulf of Mexico.

title: 15/23: Lifting chains parted – hydrogen embrittlement
description: On a vessel involved in project demobilisation, three of four lifting chains on a load parted while the load was being lifted.

title: 15/23: Davit hook failures
description: A member reports two separate instances where a workboat davit hook, and life raft davit hook components, have failed.

title: 15/23: Sheave became detached during lifting operations
description: During recovery operations of marine geophysical sensors, a sheave parted from a swivel connection on the A-frame

title: 15/23: Near miss: Personnel transfer basket hit structure
description: While transferring two personnel to a platform using the vessel crane, the base bumper of the personnel transfer basket came into contact with the helipad netting rail of the platform

title: 15/23: BSEE: A warning on tagline entanglement
description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 461 relating to recent tagline entanglements which have resulted in several High Potential near misses

title: 14/23: MAIB: High pressure oil leak causes a fire in the engine room
description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published Safety Digest 1/2023, consisting of lessons from recent Marine Accident Reports. IMCA has reviewed the digest and here passes on for members interest some but not all of the incidents in it.

title: 14/23: MAIB: Gantry crane wire parted causing injury
description: A gantry crane hoist wire parted causing a load to drop, causing injury and damage to equipment

title: 14/23: MAIB: A heavy sheave fell over causing an LTI
description: A bosun suffered a broken leg when a heavy sheave he was trying to manoeuvre, fell against him

title: 14/23: MAIB: Who is in control?
description: Control was lost of a vessel and it almost ran aground. Fortunately, the crew were able to regain control before the vessel (a ferry) grounded, and the voyage continued safely.

title: 14/23: MAIB: Lithium-ion battery fire
description: Water got into lithium-ion batteries in equipment for use subsea, causing an explosion

title: 13/23: Loss of redundancy in diving bell launch and recovery (LARS) PLC system
description: During vessel transit to an offshore field, Dive Technicians on a routine walkaround noticed an alarm from the dive bell Launch and Recovery System (LARS). Investigation indicated loss of automatic (LARS) PLC redundancy caused by failure of one of the PLC fibre optic processor synchronisation links. This resulted in the loss of normal operation and increased the risk of single point failure of the LARS.

title: 13/23: Hand injury in medical airlock
description: A Life Support Technician (LST) suffered a finger injury whilst operating the medical airlock (“Med-lock”) on a dive chamber

title: 13/23: Painter line snapped and hit crew member in the face
description: A painter line snapped during towing operations; the flying end struck a worker in the face and destroyed his safety glasses.

title: 13/23: MSF: Disposable vape self-ignition
description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has published Safety Alert 23-03 relating to an incident where an e-cigarette (“vape”) caused a small fire

title: 13/23: Hand injury while using manual torque tool
description: A Project Engineer injured his hand while using a manual torque wrench with force multiplier attached

title: 12/23: Differential pressure: Dummy choke ejected close to divers
description: A dummy choke insert was ejected from a water injection (WI) tree by force of differential pressure, while two divers were working nearby; neither diver was in the direct line of fire; both were unharmed

title: 12/23: Crane boom stopper fell to main deck
description: A knuckle boom stopper pad fell to the main deck directly below the knuckle boom; no personnel were injured - however, there was potential for serious or fatal injury

title: 12/23: Fire alarm activation in engine room
description: A supply vessel was operating within the 500m safety zone of an offshore platform when fire broke out in the engine room, causing a little damage but no harm to personnel. An alarm activated on the vessel’s fire alarm control panel, indicating a fire in the starboard side engine room cement compartment.

title: 12/23: BSEE: Swing rope transfers
description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 456 relating to the dangers inherent to swing rope transfers. The BSEE notes that “personnel transfers using swing ropes and baskets present a considerable risk for offshore workers.” The use of swing ropes is not permitted in some parts of the world.

title: 12/23: Close approach of AHTS vessel to offshore rig
description: During anchor handling operations for an offshore rig, the stern of an Anchor Handling Tug Supply (AHTS) vessel was pulled to starboard, resulting in a bow side close approach to a mooring line

title: 11/23: Uncontrolled movement of spreader bar
description: A vessel was set up alongside a barge in preparation for the subsea deployment of a 16″ (40cm) spool. The spreader bar sea-fastenings were removed by the deck crew and as the crane raised the rigging, the spreader bar rotated uncontrollably causing it to fall from its supports, with the forward end landing on deck and aft end landing on the spool

title: 11/23: Inspection notice from Crosby on certain products
description: The Crosby Group has asked IMCA to circulate the following information as part of a Safety Flash

title: 11/23: Equipment starts unexpectedly
description: A high-voltage AC unit was locked out / tagged out for routine maintenance by three mechanics, but started up unexpectedly

title: 11/23: Near Miss: Steam and water released from filter
description: Steam and water were unexpectedly released from a filter when a mechanic was cleaning out strainers from a boiler circulation pump

title: 11/23: Maintenance and control of fire doors
description: A Member has discovered instances of mandatory fire doors onboard their vessels being in a poor state of maintenance, and in some cases modified to alter the closing mechanism or tied back to prevent closing

title: 10/23: BSEE: Person injured when safety mechanisms failed
description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Alert 455 relating to an incident in which a third-party contract operator sandblasting offshore was injured when a temporary air dryer used for sandblasting operations recoiled and broke the safety cable.

title: 10/23: Dropped spanner falls 15 m
description: During work at height, a spanner became disconnected from its DROPS protection lanyard whilst crew were working in an area outside the installed protective netting. The spanner then fell to deck 15 metres below.

title: 10/23: Equipment damage: Dropped object from tiltable lay system
description: During function testing of a tensioner on a pipelay system, a bracket weighing 10.5 kg fell 16 m to deck. The tensioner doors had to be moved into the firing line, closed, and then retracted to the parked position.

title: 10/23: Near Miss: Personnel nearly struck by rotating chain attached to flexible pipe
description: During a transfer of the second end of a 4" (10 cm) production flexible, the production flexible began rotating due to residual torsion that had built up within the line. A 16.5te chain attached to the pull-in head also began spinning. Two nearby crew members who were observing the operation were almost struck by the spinning chain.

title: 10/23: Near miss – Messroom fridge fell over during rough seas
description: During transit through heavy seas, a fridge tore loose from the messroom wall and fell on its side.

title: 09/23: LTI finger injury during mooring operations
description: An AB got his left index finger trapped between a bitt and a mooring rope, resulting in a broken finger and 45 days off work. The incident occurred during un-mooring at the end of a ship-to-ship refuelling operation.

title: 09/23: Crew member trapped his left index finger in watertight door
description: A visual alarm on the bridge indicated that a watertight door near one of the engine rooms was open. Following this, during testing of the watertight door, a fitter’s left index finger was pinched between the moving door edge and door frame, causing small abrasions to the index finger.

title: 09/23: Hand injury from portable grinder
description: During flowline fabrication work at a spool base, a subcontract worker received a 3cm laceration to the hand while using a portable grinder

title: 09/23: Cut and bruise to right hand whilst pressure testing
description: A technician was pressure testing hydraulic hoses when a release of pressure occurred, knocking his hand onto the wall of the test kit, resulting in a laceration to the palm and a bruise to the back of his right hand.

title: 09/23: LTI: Hand injury in galley
description: In a vessel alongside at Christmas, the cook was preparing meat when his knife slipped and jabbed the top left part of the palm of his left hand, causing a serious laceration

title: 08/23: Serious LTI – Crew member slipped on deck breaking his leg
description: Three engineering crew members were involved in the manual handling of a bunker hose from an upper storage area to a lower deck storage area accessed via a spiral staircase. One of the engineers slipped on a greasy area of the deck breaking his right leg (fibula or calf bone) in the fall.

title: 08/23: Head injury when crew member fell over in bathroom during heavy weather
description: A vessel crew member lost balance, tripped and hit his head against the towel rail in his cabin bathroom while the vessel was rolling violently; five stitches were required to close the wound

title: 08/23: Person slipped when exiting bathroom into cabin
description: A crew member stepped out of the bathroom onto the cabin mat, when the mat slipped resulting in the crew member falling backwards, striking his lower back on the base of the bathroom door frame.

title: 08/23: Leak of oil-based mud
description: A vessel was preparing to transfer oil-based mud to the shore base. The shore base team began pressure testing their hose to ensure there was no leakage, but during the test about 20-25 litres of mud came out of the tank ventilation.

title: 08/23: Life raft secured incorrectly on cradle
description: During an onshore visit to a vessel, a life raft was observed to be attached/connected incorrectly to the life raft cradle. The life raft painter rope was connected to the cradle instead of to the weak link on the Hydrostatic Release Unit.

title: 07/23: Lift bag near miss
description: During the over-boarding of a spool, a lift bag while being inflated, ascended through the engineered rigging arrangement and was caught by the contingency rigging. Our Member considered this incident to have had the potential for a serious injury or fatality.

title: 07/23: Finger crushed under Tether Management System (TMS) protection guard
description: A worker suffered a crushed finger when the protection guard of a Saab Seaeye TMS8 Tether Management System fell on their finger. The worker was closing and securing the protection guard and lost grip on the guard.

title: 07/23: Sudden and uncontrollable move of A&R head
description: Abandonment and Recovery (A&R) head was being prepared for welding at the end of offshore pipeline installation operations. As final adjustments were being made, the A&R head assembly was moved upwards and then ejected in an uncontrolled manner from the pipe end.

title: 06/23: Ineffective Crane Stinger Hook Pin Installation (BSEE)
description: The United States Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published Safety Report 452 relating to a high-potential dropped object incident on a Gulf of Mexico energy facility

title: 06/23: Poor control of work in dry dock
description: A member reports several cases of hot work and other activities being conducted by contractors on a vessel hull during dry dock/maintenance activities, in which the work was not fully or appropriately under the control of vessel management

title: 06/23: Battery explosion during routine maintenance

title: 06/23: Near miss: Foreign body in diver’s helmet, resulting in fall of gas pressure
description: During a routine dive at a depth of 18 m (60’), the diver reported to the Dive Supervisor a drop in breathing gas pressure; on returning to the vessel and removing the helmet, a foreign body was found in the demand valve chamber section of the helmet regulator

title: 06/23: Compressor fire

title: 05/23: LTI: Person crushed in watertight door

title: 05/23: LTI: Finger crushed while moving mobile gantry crane
description: A crew member suffered a crushed index finger during manual handling of heavy equipment.

title: 05/23: LTI: Crew member crushed finger when opening fire flap

title: 05/23: High potential incident: Person struck by Yokohama fender

title: 05/23: LTI: Carbon Monoxide (CO) poisoning during Oxy-Acetylene brazing

title: 09/22 UK HSE: worker died following fall from crane platform
description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) has prosecuted a company after an electrician died in a fall of approximately eight metres when an access panel on the raised walkway of an overhead crane gave way beneath him.

title: 09/22 Riggers struck/trapped by pipe section

title: 08/22 Mooring near miss: Guide roller pin suffered material failure

title: 08/22 American P&I Club: Fire Started from cutting torch work

title: 08/22 NTSB: Dangerous engine failure – improper torquing

title: 08/22 MSF: Unsafe Cargo Transfer Using Pallets

description: The UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) has prosecuted a civil engineering company after a worker suffered life threatening injuries after falling 15 metres when a platform he was working on unexpectedly collapsed.

title: 07/22 MAIB: Unexploded ordnance – subsea explosion causes injury and damage
description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) has published its Accident Report 1/2022 into a subsea explosion which damaged crab potting vessel Galwad-Y-Mor on 15 December 2020.

title: 07/22 MAIB: Flooding, capsize and foundering of small vessel after issues with towing wires

title: 07/22 Overcoming Language Barriers

title: 06/22 Fatal fall from collapsing scaffolding on a merchant vessel

title: 06/22 Line of fire: pinched finger between door and frame

The Provisions crane was inspected after impact and mechanical damage was found on the slewing gear and pinion gear.

title: 15/20: Positive observation: Plexiglass shields installed in company shared vehicles
description: Following vehicle cleaning and disinfection protocol an additional initiative to protect drivers and passengers from COVID-19 during the pandemic is the installation of protective plexiglass shields in all company shared vehicles.

title: 15/20: COVID-19: Positive observation – maintaining social distancing during toolbox talks and meetings
description: The local mooring department of a contractor member has enforced strict physical distancing in external areas for toolbox talks (TBT) and other operational meetings.

title: 15/20: Ignited hand sanitiser

title: 14/20: Lifting operations: Wire hoist rope failure
14/20: Fire in engine room and subsequent collision with structure on transport barge
description: During the tow of a structure to location, a fire occurred in the engine room of the tow tug. This led to a blackout resulting in a collision with the structure on the transport barge.

title: 14/20: LTI: Worker lost his thumb
description: During drilling operations, a worker got his thumb caught under a part of a drill being lowered into position, resulting in the amputation of the thumb just above the knuckle.

title: 14/20: LTI: Near miss: Dropped clump weight
description: A clump weight fell approximately 30 m to deck and landed around a metre from where a rigger was working

title: 14/20: Vessel gangway rolled off platform tower and fell to the quayside in high wind
description: During stormy weather, there were sudden and violent gusts of wind of greater than 50 knots, resulting in a vessel alongside being pushed off the quay. This resulted in the gangway rolling off the platform tower and falling approximately 5.2m to the quay. The vessel’s side of the gangway remained attached to the vessel. There was no-one nearby at the time; no-one was harmed; however, the incident had the potential to cause fatal injury.

title: 13/20: Recent UK MAIB investigations (shifting of cargo and loss of cargo)
description: An agitator in a mud tank started up when an employee of a third-party contractor working in the tank was in the way. He was hit by the agitator paddle in his lower back and fell to the tank floor.

title: 13/20: Grounding of ro-ro freight vessel Seatruck Performance
description: The UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB ) has released Accident Investigation Report 4/2020 into the grounding of a freight vessel.

title: 13/20: Vessel flooding incident
description: A vessel suffered flooding and loss of integrity, caused by sea water ingress into the engine room, due to a hole developing in the box cooler bulkhead.

title: 13/20: UK HSE: Worker fell into lift shaft – safety controls bypassed
description: a 34-year-old employee was moving a loaded lift trolley in the tool department of a hangar when he fell into the lift shaft to the bottom floor and suffered life-changing injuries

title: 09/20: Potential for diver injury operating a hand-held torque wrench

title: 12/20: Chain hoist failure resulting in a serious near miss

title: 12/20: Worker fell from height and suffered life changing injuries
description: A worker was paralysed from the waist down when he fell 3.4 metres to the bottom of a ships hold

title: 12/20: Near miss: Engine room hatch left open without barriers

title: 12/20: Agitator started moving during mud tank cleaning – leading to injury

title: 10/20: Marine Safety Forum: Two incidents relating to fast rescue craft

title: 30/19: Diver trapped by anchor chain

title: 30/19: Failed shackle on vessel life raft
description: There was a failure of two stainless steel “D” shackles forming part of a life raft hydrostatic release assembly on a vessel.

title: 30/19: Uncontrolled movement of retractable gangway

description: One morning the crew of a workboat noticed an old television set floating in the sea near their work area. They decided to take it on-board in order to prevent it from potentially causing damage to a passing yacht or fishing boat.

title: 30/19: Unknown floating objects in 500m safety zone

title: 27/19: High potential near miss: Guide cone funnel dropped
description: An umbilical termination head (UTH) guide cone funnel fell from its sleeve connected to the UTH body. The UTH was the 2nd end of the umbilical. It had been lifted over the vertical lay system (VLS) tower and was being prepared for deployment when the incident occurred. The UTH guide cone funnel weighed approx. 500kg and fell more than 4m towards the moonpool doors.

title: 27/19: Hand injury during lift operations

The crane outrigger stabiliser pads (1.2T x 4) used to distribute the load from the outriggers were repositioned one at a time using a counterbalance forklift truck (FLT) and placed onto timber blocks to allow the removal of the forks.

title: 25/19: Lithium batteries: Fire following the failure of a helicopter start power unit

description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) reports an incident in which a crewman slipped and fell during lifting operations.

title: 19/17: LTI: Injury to right wrist
description: Someone using a power tool suffered a serious injury to the right wrist when the drill got out of control.

title: 19/17: LTI: Crush injury to middle and index finger
description: Riggers on a vessel were moving heavy deck plates (2.45 m x 1.2 m x 5 mm, weighing 114 kg) when one of them got his hand caught, causing a crush injury.

title: 19/17: Two cases of hand injuries – UK HSE

title: 18/17: High potential incident: Fast rescue craft capsized
description: Four people were thrown into the sea and work equipment damaged or lost when a fast rescue craft capsized while conducting a seismic survey.

title: 18/17: Painter parted during small boat operations
description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) reports an incident in which the forward painter quick release on a fast rescue craft (FRC) parted during recovery of the boat. Three crew members were in the FRC.

title: 18/17: Near miss: Failure of subsea lifting equipment
description: A dummy spool connected to two lift bags made a rapid and uncontrolled ascent to the surface.

title: 18/17: Near miss: Single wire strand protruded from original lay
description: During deployment of the bell and clump weight from a vessel for subsea inspection of a riser line, it was observed that a single wire strand protruded from original lay (‘high stranding’).

title: 18/17: Parting of hawser and bulk cargo hose during tandem mooring
description: During at-sea bunkering operations between two vessels, a mooring line parted and then a fuel hose parted also.

description: During a routine marine inspection of a vessel it was observed that rope lines had been attached to the mooring winch control levers to facilitate ‘remote’ operation of the winches.

title: 17/17: Fall from height – LTI
description: A supervisor fell 7 metres through an upper deck hatch on a vessel alongside, suffering injuries that required surgery and physiotherapy and several months away from work.

title: 17/17: Fall from height during yard visit
description: A yard worker fell 4 m from the main deck to a mezzanine deck, suffering a compression fracture in his right ankle.

title: 17/17: Crewman found collapsed – Seasickness
description: A trainee member of the crew was found lying unconscious on the deck between two cement tanks.

title: 17/17: Worker fainted and was injured during tanker operations in a tropical climate
description: After working in a crouched position on hoses aboard a tanker, a worker stood up and subsequently fainted.

title: 17/17: Worker suffers hand injury
description: The UK Health & Safety Executive (UK HSE) reports that a company was fined after a worker suffered a serious hand injury after a machinery incident.

title: 17/17: Worker severely burnt following oxygen explosion
description: The UK HSE reports that an engineering company was fined after a worker suffered life changing injuries after an oxygen pipe exploded in front of him.

title: 17/17: Stored energy – Worker scalded when hot ash dropped into water
description: The UK HSE reports that an engineering company was fined after a worker suffered life changing injuries after an oxygen pipe exploded in front of him.

title: 16/17: LTI: Hand injury resulting from clothing catching on door
description: A heavy door closed hard on a crew member's hand, injuring his thumb

title: 16/17: LTI: Finger injury during pilot ladder preparation
description: An Ordinary Seaman was injured while rigging the pilot ladder during arrival in port.

title: 16/17: LTI: Crewman burnt in fire following release of flammable gas from hand rail
description: While drilling into a handrail, a mechanic suffered burns which required time in hospital and days away from work.

title: 16/17: Fuel spray fire – Déjà vu: Prepare and prevent it from happening to you!
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has published Marine Safety Alert 06-17 to bring attention to ‘yet another fuel spray fire’. The USCG notes that “these types of incidents, involving fuel leakages contacting hot surfaces and igniting, happen too frequently and have been a focus of various marine safety organizations such as the IMO for many years.”

title: 16/17: Chemical spill leads to costly deck replacement
description: The USCG has published Marine Safety Alert 01-17 relating to hazards from chemical spills.

title: 16/17 LTI: Burn to hand while working in laundry
description: LTI: Burn to hand while working in laundry

title: 15/17: Equipment failure leading to crane collapse
description: Daily soundings of fresh water tanks on a vessel revealed that they were emptying fast – 35 tonnes over 24 hours.

title: 15/17: Near-miss: Fault spotted in subsea lifting wire
description: During diving operations at 10 msw, it was noticed that there was a slight gap in the lay of the diver launch and recovery (LARS) clump weight wire.

title: 15/17: High potential near-miss: Mooring rope parted
description: Mooring buoy rope parted while the vessel was moored.

title: 15/17: Collared eyebolts as lifting equipment
description: NOPSEMA has published Alert 64 relating to the failure of collared eyebolts when used for lifting.

title: 15/17: Near-miss: Snagged lifting bridle
description: The MSF has published Safety Alert 17-03 in which lifting rigging got snagged on an open top mini basket type unit.

title: 14/17: Near-miss: Broken chain on self-propelled hyperbaric lifeboat (SPHL) recovery rigging
description: Two near misses have occurred during diving operations.

title: 14/17: Both anchors lost due to chain fouling
description: A vessel had used both anchors whilst waiting for 3 days off the coast. Both chains were fouled and could not be cleared by the vessel. External assistance was provided but owing to the weather and sea conditions, the anchors could not be cleared, and both chains had to be cut. Attempts at retrieval of the anchors from the seabed were unsuccessful.

title: 14/17: Engine room emergency hatch damage
description: The engine room emergency hatch of an anchor handling tug supply (AHTS) vessel was damaged while towing a barge

title: 14/17: Failure of casting: Foundation brackets for steering gear
description: Damage was reported to the steering gear hydraulic ram foundation brackets connecting the ram to the structure of the vessel. The foundation bracket casting failed.

title: 14/17: Huge leak discovered in fresh water system
description: Daily soundings of fresh water tanks on a vessel revealed that they were emptying fast – 35 tonnes over 24 hours.

title: 13/17: LTI: Finger injury sustained handling heavy shackle pin
description: A crew member's left index finger was nipped between the head of the shackle and the body of the shackle. This resulted in a serious injury to the index finger of the left hand.

title: 13/17 Person accidentally drank hazardous substance: Unmarked bottle
description: A third-party agent on board a vessl during port clearance formalities drank from a mineral water bottle which instead of mineral water contained a small quantity of diluted bleaching liquid.

title: 13/17: Drill bit snapped: Finger injury sustained
description: A crewman was using an electric drill to fix a broom head to a broom stick, when the drill bit snapped off, causing the drill to slip, penetrating the crew member's safety glove and slightly dislodging the nail from his thumb.

title: 13/17: LTI: Tugger winch incident (MSF)
description: The Marine Safety Forum (MSF) has issued Safety Alert 17-01 about an incident in which an Able Seaman's foot was crushed while operating the tugger winch.

title: 13/17: Fatal fall aboard the tanker Marinor
description: The Accident Investigation Branch of Norway (AIBN) has published incident 17-04 on the fatal fall of a seafarer on board a Norwegian registered tanker, Marinor.

title: 12/17: How PPE works: Fire and thermal protection
description: The US Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) has published a report of a fire on an offshore production platform in the Gulf of Mexico, resulting in burn injuries to three workers.

title: 12/17: Galley fire: Failure to follow stove/oven installation instructions
description: The United States Coastguard (USCG) has published Marine Safety Alert 02-17, relating to a fire on an offshore platform.

title: 12/17: Dangerous modifications found within a gas valve unit room
description: The USCG has issued Safety Alert 05-17 to warn of a potentially dangerous situation involving modifications within gas valve unit (GVU) rooms aboard a liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier.

title: 12/17: Battery fire
description: In the early hours of the morning during a period of adverse weather the fire alarm in the vessel battery locker was activated.

title: 12/17: Catastrophic fire and explosion on nearby vessel
description: A vessel was double-banked alongside engaged with routine maintenance jobs, when a fire broke out on a vessel transporting a petroleum product which was berthed alongside at a berth 130 m away.

title: 12/17: Near-miss: Fire hazard from leaking fuel supply line
description: A potential fire hazard was discovered, caused by a failed fuel pipe connection on the supply line to the main engines.

title: 11/17: Dropped object injury: Equipment shifted when it was incorrectly unsecured
description: On a cable laying vessel, a cable quadrant had been rigged on the bulwarks, seated in a pedestal mounting and secured via lashings on the outboard side.

title: 11/17: LTI as a result of a load dropped from lifting magnet
description: A load dropped from a permanent lifting magnet hit a person’s hand resulting in an LTI.

title: 11/17: Dropped object: Lay tower adjuster leg pin
description: The securing pin from a tiltable lay system (TLS) adjuster leg, weighing 600 kg, fell 16 m to deck.

title: 11/17: Near-miss: Multiple potential dropped objects discovered during loading of spooling unit
description: After lifting operations were completed, a platform reported that multiple potential dropped objects (total 19 items) had been identified on the spooling unit.

title: 11/17: High potential near-miss: Incorrectly secured overhead equipment
description: During operations, it was observed that the connecting shackle pins on two separate items of overhead equipment (fall arrest inertia reels) were loose and could have become detached. Had any of this equipment fallen, it could have struck someone underneath with potentially fatal consequences.

title: 10/17: More than a dropped object – The need for vigilance during cargo operations

title: 10/17: Unsecured cargo inside containers
description: UK Step Change in Safety has published a ‘Safety Moment’ describing an incident in which a car travelling along a road near a port was struck by an object.

title: 10/17: Line parting as a result of socket failure during grapnel operations

title: 10/17: LTI: Contact with refrigerant gas causing hand injury
